Scenario selected from recent review queue evidence: agent-inbox had fresh programmatic QA findings on 2026-05-16. Evidence inspected: README.md, docs/SEAMS.md, docs/PROBLEMS.md, docs tree, requirements list, API/UI/CLI file structure, API services/handlers file inventory, UI component/hook/lib inventory, and representative files api/services/interfaces.go, api/services/completion.go, api/domain/types.go, api/services/tool_registry_types.go. Finding: material architecture documentation/structure drift. Agent Inbox README describes the product as inbox + dispatcher + chat timeline, but there is no stable architecture doc at docs/concepts/ARCHITECTURE.md or docs/internal/ARCHITECTURE.md. docs/SEAMS.md is mostly async-tracker-centric and says the domain layer is api/domain plus api/services types, while the current implementation has many product domains in generic buckets: handlers for chat/message branching/labels/settings/templates/tools/skills/usage/uploads/async status/AI streaming/agent mode; services for completion/async tracking/prompt sync/templates/storage/skill suggestion/tool registry/tool persistence/model registry/reconciliation; UI product behavior under components/chat, components/settings, hooks, and lib API wrappers. Maturity assessment: docs Level 0-1 for macro architecture (README mental model exists, durable architecture map missing), API Level 2-3 for some domain-owned implementation but with generic services package as the main ownership bucket, UI Level 2 with feature-ish subfolders but no stable domain map, CLI Level 2 with domain command groups. Non-trivial impact: future agents cannot reliably infer where new chat, tool-dispatch, template, settings, or agent-mode behavior belongs from stable docs, increasing the chance of more growth in generic services/hooks/components. Backlog created: execute/agent-inbox-screaming-architecture-domain-map. Draft plan included: add domain map and shared infrastructure map, update SEAMS to current responsibility zones, record concrete follow-up moves in PROBLEMS, then make one small high-confidence structural relocation only after docs are aligned. No bugs filed; this was structural scope, not broken behavior.

1. The CLI supports a hidden limit/pagination option but help omits it. Rejected: passing `--limit 10` fails as an unknown flag.

Partially rejected: status filters can reduce output when the user already knows the desired status, but broad list inspection remains a normal workflow and currently returns 196 execute items / 1,358 lines.
